name: Northeast India
metaTitle: Clinic & Hospital Management Software in Northeast India | Lucoze
metaDescription: Cloud HMS and EMR for clinics and hospitals across Guwahati, Silchar, Imphal and Agartala. ABHA at first visit, DPDP 2023 ready, all data in Indian data centres.
eyebrow: For clinics & hospitals in Northeast India
lead: Cloud clinic and hospital management for the Northeast — one platform for records, billing, lab and pharmacy, and honest about what we can and can't do yet. Free 14-day trial, and most practices are live in about 14 days.
intro: The Northeast runs on long distances, and patients routinely travel to Guwahati for care they can't get closer to home. Lucoze keeps records, appointments, GST billing, lab and pharmacy on one cloud platform that runs on ordinary broadband or mobile data — no on-premise server to buy, no IT team to keep it alive. Our team is in Konnagar, West Bengal, so we built support to work remotely-first: video onboarding, hands-on data migration, and WhatsApp that reaches you wherever you are — with on-site help reserved for larger hospital rollouts.
points: A cloud platform kept lightweight, so a clinic in Jorhat or Aizawl runs it on ordinary broadband or mobile data — no heavy on-premise server to buy or maintain.
Records, appointments, GST billing, lab and pharmacy in one place — no juggling separate registers across your clinic or hospital.
Create and link ABHA numbers under Ayushman Bharat (PMJAY) and state schemes right at registration, ready for claims and referrals.
Every record sits in Indian data centres under DPDP 2023, and you can export to CSV or PDF any time — no lock-in.
localContext: Lucoze's service area spans Assam, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura and the wider Northeast — Guwahati, Dibrugarh, Silchar and Jorhat in Assam, plus Imphal, Agartala, Aizawl and Shillong. The languages here are many: Assamese and English, Bengali across the Barak Valley around Silchar, and Meitei, Mizo, Kokborok and Khasi beyond. Our UI rolls out in Hindi first (Q3 2026), then Bengali, then Odia, so full Assamese screens aren't here yet. What is here today: multilingual patient search across Bengali, Devanagari and Latin, plus printable local-language cheat-sheets your front desk can pin up. We'd rather be honest about the gap than pretend it's closed. Support is remote-first, with on-site help for larger hospital rollouts.

faqs.q: Does Lucoze need a fast internet connection?
faqs.a: Lucoze is cloud-based and kept lightweight, so it runs on ordinary broadband or mobile data common across the Northeast — no expensive on-premise server. It isn't an offline system, so a working connection is needed; we keep the app efficient and stay reachable on WhatsApp if you hit trouble.

faqs.q: Where is our patient data stored?
faqs.a: In Indian data centres, under India's DPDP Act 2023. Nothing leaves the country, and you can export your records to CSV or PDF whenever you want — there's no lock-in if you ever decide to leave.

faqs.q: Which Northeast languages does Lucoze support?
faqs.a: The UI rolls out in Hindi first (Q3 2026), then Bengali, then Odia — full Assamese screens aren't available yet. Today you get multilingual patient search across Bengali, Devanagari and Latin, plus printable local-language cheat-sheets for your staff.
